The optional icon attribute accepts an emoji or Notion Icon, such as icon="icons/document_gray". Custom emoji: :emoji_name: Page: Title IMPORTANT: A tag represents a subpage (child page) on the current page. WARNING: Using with an existing page URL will MOVE that page into this page as a subpage. Removing that tag from the content will REMOVE that child page from the current page. If moving is not intended use the block instead. Folder: Title A tag represents an existing folder. Use the URL with loadFolder (or fetch in MCP) to read the folder's immediate children, then follow nested URLs to continue traversing. Preserve existing folder tags unless intentionally moving or deleting the folder. Folders cannot be created from Markdown. Database: Title Provide either url or data-source-url attribute: - If 'url' is an existing database URL, including it here will MOVE that database into the current page. If you just want to mention an existing database, use instead. - If 'data-source-url' is an existing data source URL, creates a linked database view. The 'inline' attribute toggles how the database is displayed in the UI. If set to "true", the database is fully visible and interactive on the page. If set to "false", the database is displayed as a sub-page. If you try to set inline to an invalid value, it will default to "false". The 'wiki' attribute indicates whether this database is a wiki. Wiki databases have wiki="true". When creating pages in a wiki database, you MUST use parent type "page" with the wiki's page URL instead of parent type "dataSource". Wiki pages must be created under the database page, not the data source directly. There is no 'Data Source' block type. Data Sources are always inside a Database, and only Databases can be inserted into a Page. Audio: File: Caption Embed (renders an HTML attachment file inline in a sandboxed iframe): Caption "HTML", "HTML block", "HTML artifact", and "HTML embed" all mean an HTML attachment rendered with . Never create one as a code block or file block. Always use for HTML attachment files For files created by the MCP create-attachment tool, use its returned file-upload:// source as the src value. The source is resolved and attached when create-pages or update-page saves the block. Keep the returned file upload ID if you need to retrieve the text later with download-attachment. For files uploaded through the MCP create-file-upload flow, use the upload response's suggested_markdown directly in create-pages or update-page content. To attach the upload to a comment, include suggested_markdown on a separate line in create-comment markdown; comments support up to three file attachments. Image: ![Caption](URL) {color?="Color"} PDF: Caption Video: (Note that source URLs can either be compressed URLs, such as src="{{1}}", or full URLs, such as src="example.com". Full URLs enclosed in curly brackets, like src="{{https://example.com}}" or src="{{example.com}}", do not work.) Table of contents: Synced block: The original source for a synced block. When creating a new synced block, do not provide the URL. After inserting the synced block into a page, the URL will be provided. Children Note: When creating new synced blocks, omit the url attribute - it will be auto-generated. When reading existing synced blocks, the url attribute will be present. Synced block reference: A reference to a synced block. The synced block must already exist and url must be provided. You can directly update the children of the synced block reference and it will update both the original synced block and the synced block reference. If content is unavailable due to permissions, a non-editable notice may be included via the optional notice attribute. Children Meeting notes: Rich text (meeting title) AI-generated summary of the notes + transcript User notes Transcript of the audio (cannot be edited) - The tag contains a raw transcript and cannot be edited by AI, but it can be edited by a user. - When creating new meeting notes blocks, you must omit the and tags. - Only include in a new meeting notes block if the user is SPECIFICALLY requesting note content. - Attempting to include or edit will result in an error. - All content within , , and tags must be indented at least one level deeper than the tag. Custom blocks: Omit url when creating a new instance. Readback adds its instance URL; preserve that URL when editing, reordering, or moving an existing instance. Place the self-closing tag on its own line. It references a saved definition in the destination workspace and inherits its bindings; it does not contain rendered content or instance binding overrides. New placements and definition changes require a live definition readable by the caller. Retaining the same existing instance and definition does not require fresh definition access, even if the definition was deleted. Adding another instance still requires authorization. Public API and MCP requests reject definition-key, which is reserved for App deployments. Reading or placing an existing definition through Markdown does not require separate workspace enablement; definition creation remains in private alpha. {"id":"3f5d67cd-0a05-805b-8023-c53570998144","title":"Hackathon Page","text":"Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3f5d67cd0a05805b8023c53570998144 as of 2026-10-10T15:38:42.580Z: {"title":"Hackathon Page"} null Ideas; Recruitment agent, use voice chat to build profile, build something that actually matches you to jobs, filter out shit, personal recommendation about how you are feeling, what to do, plans, organise something voice chat, takes in info, asks lots of questions to get information on your profile, finds out what is important to you and builds on that, creates dashbaord for you track habits, plans, jobs, etc --- # AI Conversation Coach — Four-Hour Hackathon Build Plan **Date:** 10 October 2026 **Concept:** An AI role-play simulator for conversations people find difficult. The user speaks out loud to a cartoon/metaverse-style character that answers naturally, challenges them, and gives specific feedback at the end. ## Product pitch **Practice the conversations that matter — before having them for real.** Examples: - Job interview with a realistic hiring manager - Asking a boss for a raise - Breaking up / navigating a difficult relationship conversation - Giving or receiving difficult workplace feedback - Negotiating, setting boundaries, apologising, or handling conflict - Custom user-provided scenario The differentiator is **interactive rehearsal and useful feedback**, not photorealistic avatar technology. ## Implementation status — 10 October 2026 Checked items below mean implemented in the current local code, not fully approved for a live demo. The core voice loop, animated sunflower, scenario selection and feedback UI are present. Current tests expose profile/report contract mismatches and browser regressions; final demo acceptance remains open. ### Still to finish / verify - [ ] Reconcile profile/report implementation with its tests, resolve typecheck errors, and verify report saving for all scenarios. - [ ] Rehearse the complete two-minute Ask for a Raise demo with a real microphone, three turns, spoken replies and useful final feedback; check echo, latency and restart. - [ ] If demonstrating on a public URL, implement protected voice-token issuance. Continuous voice currently permits [localhost](http://localhost) only; final recorded WAV transcription is a separate path. **Fresh audit results:** unit/API tests: 178 passed, 17 failed; browser tests: 21 passed, 6 failed; typecheck failed on profile test/API mismatches. Several browser failures use outdated labels or incompatible report fixtures; they do not by themselves prove the corresponding feature is absent. The three-turn browser test reached and displayed feedback before failing on its old restart-button label. **Verification basis:** current source and fresh automated checks; provider calls in these tests are mocked. Existing README live-provider checks are historical evidence, not a fresh physical-microphone rehearsal. Other work was changing the checkout during this audit, so this is a point-in-time snapshot. ## Scope: what we actually ship in four hours **Must have** - [x] Choose a scenario and difficulty (friendly / neutral / challenging) - [x] Display one premade cartoon avatar - [x] User speaks with live chat - [x] Gradium transcribes the user's speech - [x] Gemini generates a brief in-character response using conversation history - [x] Gradium turns the response into speech - [x] Avatar switches among idle, listening and speaking animations - [x] End Session generates a short feedback report **Originally cut / optional scope** Unchecked exclusions below are intentional scope cuts, not remaining MVP requirements. Continuous voice and reporting were subsequently added as noted. - [ ] Photorealistic lip-sync, body tracking or elaborate gestures - [ ] Authentication, payment, database or saved accounts - [x] Full-duplex voice interruptions and overlapping speech — subsequently implemented as local continuous voice with interruption handling; playback-interruption regression still needs verification. - [ ] Complex environments, multi-character scenes, multiplayer - [ ] Sophisticated analytics and long transcripts dashboard — partially exceeded: local profiles, saved transcripts, score trends, answer reviews and speech metrics exist; profile/report integration checks are still failing. Photo-to-avatar is not required for this MVP. A premade stylized character plus basic lip movement is sufficient for the demo. ## Proposed technology stack
Layer Technology Responsibility
UI Next.js + TypeScript + Tailwind Scenario picker, voice screen, results
Conversation brain Gemini Flash via @google/genai Role-play, follow-up questions, feedback
Voice recognition Gradium STT Convert user's mic audio to text
Voice generation Gradium TTS Read Gemini's answer in character
Avatar Animated 2D SVG **or** premade GLB/VRM Show idle/listening/speaking states
API orchestration Next.js route handlers Protect API keys; coordinate services
Media Browser microphone, HTMLAudioElement Capture/play voice audio
**Choice:** For a reliable four-hour build, prefer a polished animated 2D portrait. Use a premade 3D GLB/VRM only if it already loads and animates. Building an avatar engine is not the product. **Avoid Gemini Live for this particular prototype:** If Gradium must supply both STT and TTS, use Gemini for **text conversation**. Gemini Live's own native audio capabilities would duplicate part of the Gradium pipeline. ## End-to-end architecture 1. User selects scenario + difficulty. 2. Browser records one answer using push-to-talk. 3. POST recorded audio to server API route. 4. Backend sends supported audio to Gradium speech-to-text; obtains a transcript. 5. Backend sends transcript and previous conversation turns to Gemini. 6. Gemini replies as the chosen character, usually 1–3 spoken sentences; backend appends that turn to history. 7. Backend sends Gemini's reply to Gradium text-to-speech and receives audio. 8. Frontend plays the audio and switches avatar to **speaking**. 9. Playback ends; avatar returns to **idle/listening**. 10. User can repeat until they press **End Session**. 11. Gemini evaluates the transcript against a rubric and returns 2 strengths, 2 improvements and 1 suggested better response. **Conceptual flow:** User microphone → Gradium STT → Gemini Flash + history → Gradium TTS → spoken audio + animated avatar. ## Quick setup 1. Get a [Gemini API key](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey). 2. Get a [Gradium API key](https://studio.gradium.ai/). 3. Scaffold a Next.js project and install the Google GenAI SDK. 4. Keep keys on the backend. Never expose Gradium/Gemini keys through NEXT_PUBLIC environment variables. ```bash npx create-next-app@latest conversation-coach cd conversation-coach npm install @google/genai ``` Create .env.local: ```bash GEMINI_API_KEY=your_key GRADIUM_API_KEY=your_key ``` Suggested routes: - POST /api/transcribe — receive user audio; Gradium STT; return text - POST /api/converse — scenario + difficulty + conversation history + user message; Gemini; return reply - POST /api/speak — text; Gradium TTS; return playable WAV audio - POST /api/feedback — conversation transcript + scenario; Gemini; return structured feedback ## Gemini implementation example ```typescript import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai"; const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY, }); const response = await ai.models.generateContent({ model: "gemini-2.5-flash", contents: "I'd like to discuss a salary increase.", config: { systemInstruction: "You are a skeptical but fair manager. The user is practising asking for a raise. " + "Stay in character. Ask challenging but believable follow-up questions. " + "Respond in 1–3 natural spoken sentences. Do not coach until the session ends.", }, }); console.log(response.text); ``` For real conversations, send a chat session/history containing **all prior turns**, not only the latest utterance. Keep the role-play consistent with scenario, role and difficulty. Keep replies short to lower latency. ## Gradium voice integration API base: [https://api.gradium.ai](https://api.gradium.ai) - **Speech-to-text:** POST /api/post/speech/asr - **Text-to-speech:** POST /api/post/speech/tts - Follow current official REST request/response details; validate with one sample before building the whole UI. Example server-side TTS request: ```typescript const response = await fetch( "https://api.gradium.ai/api/post/speech/tts", { method: "POST", headers: { "x-api-key": process.env.GRADIUM_API_KEY!, "Content-Type": "application/json", }, body: JSON.stringify({ text: "Why do you believe you deserve a raise?", voice_id: "YTpq7expH9539ERJ", output_format: "wav", only_audio: true, }), } ); if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Gradium TTS failed"); const audio = await response.arrayBuffer(); ``` Return the WAV from the server to the browser with the correct audio content type. Choose an available voice ID from the Gradium docs/dashboard if the example changes. **Important STT gotcha:** MediaRecorder may output WebM/Opus in the browser. Do **not** label WebM as WAV. Either record/encode PCM WAV or convert correctly server-side. Parse the STT response according to the current Gradium docs (including NDJSON segments if returned), concatenating relevant recognised text. **Latency choice:** push-to-talk instead of continuous full-duplex streaming. Finish one turn, get text, generate response, synthesize and play audio, then resume listening. ## Cartoon avatar implementation **Fastest:** animated SVG / 2D character with subtle bobbing, periodic blink and a two-state mouth. Use CSS or Framer Motion if already installed. **If 3D is essential:** use one licensed premade GLB/VRM avatar + Three.js / React Three Fiber; a compatible VRM can use three-vrm for expressions. Frame the upper torso. Avoid the avatar editor entirely. Ready Player Me's former public offering should not be assumed available. Animation states: - **idle**: breathing/bobbing, occasional blink - **listening**: face forward, slight attentiveness - **speaking**: mouth toggles, small nod/head sway during TTS playback ```typescript audio.onplay = () => setIsSpeaking(true); audio.onended = () => setIsSpeaking(false); audio.onerror = () => setIsSpeaking(false); ``` This is an intentionally approximate speaking animation, not phoneme-accurate lip-sync. If there is no mouth blendshape, use an SVG mouth or simple mesh swap instead. ## Scenarios and persona instructions ### Job interview "You are an experienced interviewer assessing a candidate. Ask one question at a time. Demand specific examples and probe vague claims. Remain professional. Do not reveal a rubric or provide coaching until the session ends." ### Asking for a raise "You are the user's manager. You are skeptical but fair about salary increases. Ask for evidence of performance, impact and market value. Raise natural objections. Keep replies concise and conversational." ### Breakup or emotionally difficult conversation "You are the other party in a difficult but respectful relationship conversation. React in a believable, emotionally nuanced way while avoiding threats, manipulation or abuse. Let the user practise empathy and boundaries." ### Difficult feedback "You are a coworker receiving uncomfortable feedback. Start a little defensive, but become more receptive to clear, respectful and specific communication." ### Difficulty settings - **Friendly:** collaborative, gentle objections, lower pressure - **Neutral:** realistic responses and a few challenges - **Challenging:** probing objections, skepticism, follow-up questions without unnecessary hostility System instruction for every scenario: **Stay in character during practice; ask one question at a time; speak naturally in 1–3 sentences; do not prematurely deliver feedback.** A separate Gemini request should generate the final report. ## Interface / demo flow 1. **Landing:** "Practice difficult conversations with AI" 2. **Scenario cards:** Interview / Salary raise / Relationship / Difficult feedback / Custom 3. **Difficulty:** Friendly / Neutral / Challenging 4. **Conversation:** central cartoon avatar, animated state, push-to-talk mic button, small transcript, End Session 5. **Results:** two strengths, two improvements, recommended alternative phrasing; optionally restart at a harder difficulty Demo storyline: select **Ask for a Raise** → speak a salary request → manager challenges the justification by voice → respond once more → End Session → concise actionable report. ## Four-hour sprint checklist ### 00:00–00:45 — Gemini + skeleton UI - [x] Scaffold Next.js; create scenario picker - [x] Add /api/converse and persona prompts - [x] Verify a typed message gets an in-character Gemini response **Checkpoint:** text role-play works, even without voice. ### 00:45–01:40 — Gradium TTS - [x] Create /api/speak - [x] Turn a fixed sentence into playable speech - [x] Wire Gemini responses to automatic audio playback **Checkpoint:** click a button; character's response is heard. ### 01:40–02:35 — Microphone + STT - [x] Record short user turn - [x] Convert to compatible audio encoding - [x] Create /api/transcribe, parse recognized text - [x] Chain transcription → Gemini → TTS **Checkpoint:** complete two-way voice interaction works. ### 02:35–03:20 — Avatar animation - [x] Render one premade 2D or 3D avatar - [x] Implement idle/listening/speaking states - [x] Hook speaking state to TTS audio playback **Checkpoint:** avatar visibly responds when AI speaks. ### 03:20–04:00 — Feedback + reliability + demo - [x] Add the scenario/difficulty presets - [x] End Session report (2 strengths, 2 improvements, improved phrasing) - [x] Handle microphone denied, empty audio and failed API requests - [ ] Rehearse a complete 2-minute walkthrough **Checkpoint:** demo works from start to finish. ## What could go wrong / fallback plan - **STT audio incompatibility:** test encoding immediately; if blocked, temporarily allow typed input so the rest of the demo remains usable. - **3D avatar takes too long:** revert to a clean 2D SVG character. Animation quality is secondary. - **TTS latency:** keep Gemini replies short, use a loading/speaking state, and avoid huge transcripts per request. - **API quota or model problems:** test keys at the start, show recoverable errors, and have a prerecorded walkthrough/video only as backup for the presentation. - **Unsafe/awkward role-play:** give scenarios clear guardrails; keep relationship simulations respectful and clearly fictional. - **Privacy:** avoid storing raw recordings in MVP unless necessary; get consent if recording or keeping a transcript. ## Definition of done - [x] A user can select **Ask for a Raise** - [x] Their spoken words are recognized by Gradium - [x] Gemini responds in character based on conversation history - [x] Gradium delivers the response in a spoken voice - [x] A cartoon avatar animates when speaking - [x] User can complete at least three turns - [ ] End Session produces clear, useful feedback - [ ] One complete demo can run without editing source code or manually calling APIs ## Copy-paste prompt for Cursor / coding agent > Build a hackathon MVP called Conversation Coach using Next.js App Router, TypeScript and Tailwind. Users select an interview, salary negotiation, breakup conversation, or difficult feedback scenario. Gemini is the conversation AI, using @google/genai with gemini-2.5-flash and full multi-turn history. Gradium must handle both speech-to-text and text-to-speech using the documented REST endpoints. Implement server-side routes /api/transcribe, /api/converse, /api/speak, and /api/feedback; keep keys in GEMINI_API_KEY and GRADIUM_API_KEY server environment variables. Use browser push-to-talk recording, and ensure WAV compatibility for Gradium STT (do not send WebM marked as WAV). Parse Gradium STT responses correctly. Use Gradium TTS with WAV audio output and play it with an HTMLAudioElement. Build a playful, clean cartoon avatar UI with idle/listening/speaking states and simple mouth motion during playback. Prioritize a functional voice loop over complex 3D. Include friendly, neutral and challenging difficulty settings; keep Gemini in character with short spoken replies. Maintain conversation history. Add End Session feedback with 2 strengths, 2 improvements and a suggested better response from Gemini. Add loading, microphone and API error states. No database, authentication, payments, photo-to-avatar generation or unnecessary dependencies. Implement incrementally: text conversation first, then TTS, then STT, then avatar, then feedback. ## Documentation / links - [Gemini API keys](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey) - [Google GenAI / Gemini API](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content) - [Gradium Studio](https://studio.gradium.ai/) - [Gradium speech-to-text REST guide](https://docs.gradium.ai/guides/speech-to-text-rest) - [Gradium text-to-speech REST guide](https://docs.gradium.ai/guides/text-to-speech-rest) - [three-vrm for optional 3D avatar](https://github.com/pixiv/three-vrm) **Execution rule:** Do not spend the first two hours making the avatar pretty. First prove the voice conversation loop. The avatar is a presentation layer, not the core value. {"id":"3f5d67cd-0a05-805b-8023-c53570998144","title":"Hackathon Page","text":"Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3f5d67cd0a05805b8023c53570998144 as of 2026-10-10T15:38:42.580Z: {"title":"Hackathon Page"} null Ideas; Recruitment agent, use voice chat to build profile, build something that actually matches you to jobs, filter out shit, personal recommendation about how you are feeling, what to do, plans, organise something voice chat, takes in info, asks lots of questions to get information on your profile, finds out what is important to you and builds on that, creates dashbaord for you track habits, plans, jobs, etc --- # AI Conversation Coach — Four-Hour Hackathon Build Plan **Date:** 10 October 2026 **Concept:** An AI role-play simulator for conversations people find difficult. The user speaks out loud to a cartoon/metaverse-style character that answers naturally, challenges them, and gives specific feedback at the end. ## Product pitch **Practice the conversations that matter — before having them for real.** Examples: - Job interview with a realistic hiring manager - Asking a boss for a raise - Breaking up / navigating a difficult relationship conversation - Giving or receiving difficult workplace feedback - Negotiating, setting boundaries, apologising, or handling conflict - Custom user-provided scenario The differentiator is **interactive rehearsal and useful feedback**, not photorealistic avatar technology. ## Implementation status — 10 October 2026 Checked items below mean implemented in the current local code, not fully approved for a live demo. The core voice loop, animated sunflower, scenario selection and feedback UI are present. Current tests expose profile/report contract mismatches and browser regressions; final demo acceptance remains open. ### Still to finish / verify - [ ] Reconcile profile/report implementation with its tests, resolve typecheck errors, and verify report saving for all scenarios. - [ ] Rehearse the complete two-minute Ask for a Raise demo with a real microphone, three turns, spoken replies and useful final feedback; check echo, latency and restart. - [ ] If demonstrating on a public URL, implement protected voice-token issuance. Continuous voice currently permits [localhost](http://localhost) only; final recorded WAV transcription is a separate path. **Fresh audit results:** unit/API tests: 178 passed, 17 failed; browser tests: 21 passed, 6 failed; typecheck failed on profile test/API mismatches. Several browser failures use outdated labels or incompatible report fixtures; they do not by themselves prove the corresponding feature is absent. The three-turn browser test reached and displayed feedback before failing on its old restart-button label. **Verification basis:** current source and fresh automated checks; provider calls in these tests are mocked. Existing README live-provider checks are historical evidence, not a fresh physical-microphone rehearsal. Other work was changing the checkout during this audit, so this is a point-in-time snapshot. ## Scope: what we actually ship in four hours **Must have** - [x] Choose a scenario and difficulty (friendly / neutral / challenging) - [x] Display one premade cartoon avatar - [x] User speaks with live chat - [x] Gradium transcribes the user's speech - [x] Gemini generates a brief in-character response using conversation history - [x] Gradium turns the response into speech - [x] Avatar switches among idle, listening and speaking animations - [x] End Session generates a short feedback report **Originally cut / optional scope** Unchecked exclusions below are intentional scope cuts, not remaining MVP requirements. Continuous voice and reporting were subsequently added as noted. - [ ] Photorealistic lip-sync, body tracking or elaborate gestures - [ ] Authentication, payment, database or saved accounts - [x] Full-duplex voice interruptions and overlapping speech — subsequently implemented as local continuous voice with interruption handling; playback-interruption regression still needs verification. - [ ] Complex environments, multi-character scenes, multiplayer - [ ] Sophisticated analytics and long transcripts dashboard — partially exceeded: local profiles, saved transcripts, score trends, answer reviews and speech metrics exist; profile/report integration checks are still failing. Photo-to-avatar is not required for this MVP. A premade stylized character plus basic lip movement is sufficient for the demo. ## Proposed technology stack
Layer Technology Responsibility
UI Next.js + TypeScript + Tailwind Scenario picker, voice screen, results
Conversation brain Gemini Flash via @google/genai Role-play, follow-up questions, feedback
Voice recognition Gradium STT Convert user's mic audio to text
Voice generation Gradium TTS Read Gemini's answer in character
Avatar Animated 2D SVG **or** premade GLB/VRM Show idle/listening/speaking states
API orchestration Next.js route handlers Protect API keys; coordinate services
Media Browser microphone, HTMLAudioElement Capture/play voice audio
**Choice:** For a reliable four-hour build, prefer a polished animated 2D portrait. Use a premade 3D GLB/VRM only if it already loads and animates. Building an avatar engine is not the product. **Avoid Gemini Live for this particular prototype:** If Gradium must supply both STT and TTS, use Gemini for **text conversation**. Gemini Live's own native audio capabilities would duplicate part of the Gradium pipeline. ## End-to-end architecture 1. User selects scenario + difficulty. 2. Browser records one answer using push-to-talk. 3. POST recorded audio to server API route. 4. Backend sends supported audio to Gradium speech-to-text; obtains a transcript. 5. Backend sends transcript and previous conversation turns to Gemini. 6. Gemini replies as the chosen character, usually 1–3 spoken sentences; backend appends that turn to history. 7. Backend sends Gemini's reply to Gradium text-to-speech and receives audio. 8. Frontend plays the audio and switches avatar to **speaking**. 9. Playback ends; avatar returns to **idle/listening**. 10. User can repeat until they press **End Session**. 11. Gemini evaluates the transcript against a rubric and returns 2 strengths, 2 improvements and 1 suggested better response. **Conceptual flow:** User microphone → Gradium STT → Gemini Flash + history → Gradium TTS → spoken audio + animated avatar. ## Quick setup 1. Get a [Gemini API key](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey). 2. Get a [Gradium API key](https://studio.gradium.ai/). 3. Scaffold a Next.js project and install the Google GenAI SDK. 4. Keep keys on the backend. Never expose Gradium/Gemini keys through NEXT_PUBLIC environment variables. ```bash npx create-next-app@latest conversation-coach cd conversation-coach npm install @google/genai ``` Create .env.local: ```bash GEMINI_API_KEY=your_key GRADIUM_API_KEY=your_key ``` Suggested routes: - POST /api/transcribe — receive user audio; Gradium STT; return text - POST /api/converse — scenario + difficulty + conversation history + user message; Gemini; return reply - POST /api/speak — text; Gradium TTS; return playable WAV audio - POST /api/feedback — conversation transcript + scenario; Gemini; return structured feedback ## Gemini implementation example ```typescript import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai"; const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY, }); const response = await ai.models.generateContent({ model: "gemini-2.5-flash", contents: "I'd like to discuss a salary increase.", config: { systemInstruction: "You are a skeptical but fair manager. The user is practising asking for a raise. " + "Stay in character. Ask challenging but believable follow-up questions. " + "Respond in 1–3 natural spoken sentences. Do not coach until the session ends.", }, }); console.log(response.text); ``` For real conversations, send a chat session/history containing **all prior turns**, not only the latest utterance. Keep the role-play consistent with scenario, role and difficulty. Keep replies short to lower latency. ## Gradium voice integration API base: [https://api.gradium.ai](https://api.gradium.ai) - **Speech-to-text:** POST /api/post/speech/asr - **Text-to-speech:** POST /api/post/speech/tts - Follow current official REST request/response details; validate with one sample before building the whole UI. Example server-side TTS request: ```typescript const response = await fetch( "https://api.gradium.ai/api/post/speech/tts", { method: "POST", headers: { "x-api-key": process.env.GRADIUM_API_KEY!, "Content-Type": "application/json", }, body: JSON.stringify({ text: "Why do you believe you deserve a raise?", voice_id: "YTpq7expH9539ERJ", output_format: "wav", only_audio: true, }), } ); if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Gradium TTS failed"); const audio = await response.arrayBuffer(); ``` Return the WAV from the server to the browser with the correct audio content type. Choose an available voice ID from the Gradium docs/dashboard if the example changes. **Important STT gotcha:** MediaRecorder may output WebM/Opus in the browser. Do **not** label WebM as WAV. Either record/encode PCM WAV or convert correctly server-side. Parse the STT response according to the current Gradium docs (including NDJSON segments if returned), concatenating relevant recognised text. **Latency choice:** push-to-talk instead of continuous full-duplex streaming. Finish one turn, get text, generate response, synthesize and play audio, then resume listening. ## Cartoon avatar implementation **Fastest:** animated SVG / 2D character with subtle bobbing, periodic blink and a two-state mouth. Use CSS or Framer Motion if already installed. **If 3D is essential:** use one licensed premade GLB/VRM avatar + Three.js / React Three Fiber; a compatible VRM can use three-vrm for expressions. Frame the upper torso. Avoid the avatar editor entirely. Ready Player Me's former public offering should not be assumed available. Animation states: - **idle**: breathing/bobbing, occasional blink - **listening**: face forward, slight attentiveness - **speaking**: mouth toggles, small nod/head sway during TTS playback ```typescript audio.onplay = () => setIsSpeaking(true); audio.onended = () => setIsSpeaking(false); audio.onerror = () => setIsSpeaking(false); ``` This is an intentionally approximate speaking animation, not phoneme-accurate lip-sync. If there is no mouth blendshape, use an SVG mouth or simple mesh swap instead. ## Scenarios and persona instructions ### Job interview "You are an experienced interviewer assessing a candidate. Ask one question at a time. Demand specific examples and probe vague claims. Remain professional. Do not reveal a rubric or provide coaching until the session ends." ### Asking for a raise "You are the user's manager. You are skeptical but fair about salary increases. Ask for evidence of performance, impact and market value. Raise natural objections. Keep replies concise and conversational." ### Breakup or emotionally difficult conversation "You are the other party in a difficult but respectful relationship conversation. React in a believable, emotionally nuanced way while avoiding threats, manipulation or abuse. Let the user practise empathy and boundaries." ### Difficult feedback "You are a coworker receiving uncomfortable feedback. Start a little defensive, but become more receptive to clear, respectful and specific communication." ### Difficulty settings - **Friendly:** collaborative, gentle objections, lower pressure - **Neutral:** realistic responses and a few challenges - **Challenging:** probing objections, skepticism, follow-up questions without unnecessary hostility System instruction for every scenario: **Stay in character during practice; ask one question at a time; speak naturally in 1–3 sentences; do not prematurely deliver feedback.** A separate Gemini request should generate the final report. ## Interface / demo flow 1. **Landing:** "Practice difficult conversations with AI" 2. **Scenario cards:** Interview / Salary raise / Relationship / Difficult feedback / Custom 3. **Difficulty:** Friendly / Neutral / Challenging 4. **Conversation:** central cartoon avatar, animated state, push-to-talk mic button, small transcript, End Session 5. **Results:** two strengths, two improvements, recommended alternative phrasing; optionally restart at a harder difficulty Demo storyline: select **Ask for a Raise** → speak a salary request → manager challenges the justification by voice → respond once more → End Session → concise actionable report. ## Four-hour sprint checklist ### 00:00–00:45 — Gemini + skeleton UI - [x] Scaffold Next.js; create scenario picker - [x] Add /api/converse and persona prompts - [x] Verify a typed message gets an in-character Gemini response **Checkpoint:** text role-play works, even without voice. ### 00:45–01:40 — Gradium TTS - [x] Create /api/speak - [x] Turn a fixed sentence into playable speech - [x] Wire Gemini responses to automatic audio playback **Checkpoint:** click a button; character's response is heard. ### 01:40–02:35 — Microphone + STT - [x] Record short user turn - [x] Convert to compatible audio encoding - [x] Create /api/transcribe, parse recognized text - [x] Chain transcription → Gemini → TTS **Checkpoint:** complete two-way voice interaction works. ### 02:35–03:20 — Avatar animation - [x] Render one premade 2D or 3D avatar - [x] Implement idle/listening/speaking states - [x] Hook speaking state to TTS audio playback **Checkpoint:** avatar visibly responds when AI speaks. ### 03:20–04:00 — Feedback + reliability + demo - [x] Add the scenario/difficulty presets - [x] End Session report (2 strengths, 2 improvements, improved phrasing) - [x] Handle microphone denied, empty audio and failed API requests - [ ] Rehearse a complete 2-minute walkthrough **Checkpoint:** demo works from start to finish. ## What could go wrong / fallback plan - **STT audio incompatibility:** test encoding immediately; if blocked, temporarily allow typed input so the rest of the demo remains usable. - **3D avatar takes too long:** revert to a clean 2D SVG character. Animation quality is secondary. - **TTS latency:** keep Gemini replies short, use a loading/speaking state, and avoid huge transcripts per request. - **API quota or model problems:** test keys at the start, show recoverable errors, and have a prerecorded walkthrough/video only as backup for the presentation. - **Unsafe/awkward role-play:** give scenarios clear guardrails; keep relationship simulations respectful and clearly fictional. - **Privacy:** avoid storing raw recordings in MVP unless necessary; get consent if recording or keeping a transcript. ## Definition of done - [x] A user can select **Ask for a Raise** - [x] Their spoken words are recognized by Gradium - [x] Gemini responds in character based on conversation history - [x] Gradium delivers the response in a spoken voice - [x] A cartoon avatar animates when speaking - [x] User can complete at least three turns - [ ] End Session produces clear, useful feedback - [ ] One complete demo can run without editing source code or manually calling APIs ## Copy-paste prompt for Cursor / coding agent > Build a hackathon MVP called Conversation Coach using Next.js App Router, TypeScript and Tailwind. Users select an interview, salary negotiation, breakup conversation, or difficult feedback scenario. Gemini is the conversation AI, using @google/genai with gemini-2.5-flash and full multi-turn history. Gradium must handle both speech-to-text and text-to-speech using the documented REST endpoints. Implement server-side routes /api/transcribe, /api/converse, /api/speak, and /api/feedback; keep keys in GEMINI_API_KEY and GRADIUM_API_KEY server environment variables. Use browser push-to-talk recording, and ensure WAV compatibility for Gradium STT (do not send WebM marked as WAV). Parse Gradium STT responses correctly. Use Gradium TTS with WAV audio output and play it with an HTMLAudioElement. Build a playful, clean cartoon avatar UI with idle/listening/speaking states and simple mouth motion during playback. Prioritize a functional voice loop over complex 3D. Include friendly, neutral and challenging difficulty settings; keep Gemini in character with short spoken replies. Maintain conversation history. Add End Session feedback with 2 strengths, 2 improvements and a suggested better response from Gemini. Add loading, microphone and API error states. No database, authentication, payments, photo-to-avatar generation or unnecessary dependencies. Implement incrementally: text conversation first, then TTS, then STT, then avatar, then feedback. ## Documentation / links - [Gemini API keys](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey) - [Google GenAI / Gemini API](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content) - [Gradium Studio](https://studio.gradium.ai/) - [Gradium speech-to-text REST guide](https://docs.gradium.ai/guides/speech-to-text-rest) - [Gradium text-to-speech REST guide](https://docs.gradium.ai/guides/text-to-speech-rest) - [three-vrm for optional 3D avatar](https://github.com/pixiv/three-vrm) **Execution rule:** Do not spend the first two hours making the avatar pretty. First prove the voice conversation loop. The avatar is a presentation layer, not the core value. The user speaks out loud to a cartoon/metaverse-style character that answers naturally, challenges them, and gives specific feedback at the end. ## Product pitch **Practice the conversations that matter — before having them for real.** Examples: - Job interview with a realistic hiring manager - Asking a boss for a raise - Breaking up / navigating a difficult relationship conversation - Giving or receiving difficult workplace feedback - Negotiating, setting boundaries, apologising, or handling conflict - Custom user-provided scenario The differentiator is **interactive rehearsal and useful feedback**, not photorealistic avatar technology. ## Earlier implementation audit — superseded The earlier audit recorded 178 passing and 17 failing unit/API tests, browser regressions and typecheck errors while work was changing. The fresh unit/API and typecheck results above supersede those failures; final physical-microphone demo acceptance remains open. ## Scope: what we actually ship in four hours **Must have** - [x] Choose a scenario and difficulty (friendly / neutral / challenging) - [x] Display one premade cartoon avatar - [x] User speaks with live chat - [x] Gradium transcribes the user's speech - [x] Gemini generates a brief in-character response using conversation history - [x] Gradium turns the response into speech - [x] Avatar switches among idle, listening and speaking animations - [x] End Session generates a short feedback report **Originally cut / optional scope** Unchecked exclusions below are intentional scope cuts, not remaining MVP requirements. Continuous voice and reporting were subsequently added as noted. - [ ] Photorealistic lip-sync, body tracking or elaborate gestures - [ ] Authentication, payment, database or saved accounts - [x] Full-duplex voice interruptions and overlapping speech — subsequently implemented as local continuous voice with interruption handling; playback-interruption regression still needs verification. - [ ] Complex environments, multi-character scenes, multiplayer - [ ] Sophisticated analytics and long transcripts dashboard — partially exceeded: local profiles, saved transcripts, score trends, answer reviews and speech metrics exist; profile/report integration checks are still failing. Photo-to-avatar is not required for this MVP. A premade stylized character plus basic lip movement is sufficient for the demo. ## Proposed technology stack
Layer Technology Responsibility
UI Next.js + TypeScript + Tailwind Scenario picker, voice screen, results
Conversation brain Gemini Flash via @google/genai Role-play, follow-up questions, feedback
Voice recognition Gradium STT Convert user's mic audio to text
Voice generation Gradium TTS Read Gemini's answer in character
Avatar Animated 2D SVG **or** premade GLB/VRM Show idle/listening/speaking states
API orchestration Next.js route handlers Protect API keys; coordinate services
Media Browser microphone, HTMLAudioElement Capture/play voice audio
**Choice:** For a reliable four-hour build, prefer a polished animated 2D portrait. Use a premade 3D GLB/VRM only if it already loads and animates. Building an avatar engine is not the product. **Avoid Gemini Live for this particular prototype:** If Gradium must supply both STT and TTS, use Gemini for **text conversation**. Gemini Live's own native audio capabilities would duplicate part of the Gradium pipeline. ## End-to-end architecture 1. User selects scenario + difficulty. 2. Browser records one answer using push-to-talk. 3. POST recorded audio to server API route. 4. Backend sends supported audio to Gradium speech-to-text; obtains a transcript. 5. Backend sends transcript and previous conversation turns to Gemini. 6. Gemini replies as the chosen character, usually 1–3 spoken sentences; backend appends that turn to history. 7. Backend sends Gemini's reply to Gradium text-to-speech and receives audio. 8. Frontend plays the audio and switches avatar to **speaking**. 9. Playback ends; avatar returns to **idle/listening**. 10. User can repeat until they press **End Session**. 11. Gemini evaluates the transcript against a rubric and returns 2 strengths, 2 improvements and 1 suggested better response. **Conceptual flow:** User microphone → Gradium STT → Gemini Flash + history → Gradium TTS → spoken audio + animated avatar. ## Quick setup 1. Get a [Gemini API key](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey). 2. Get a [Gradium API key](https://studio.gradium.ai/). 3. Scaffold a Next.js project and install the Google GenAI SDK. 4. Keep keys on the backend. Never expose Gradium/Gemini keys through NEXT_PUBLIC environment variables. ```bash npx create-next-app@latest conversation-coach cd conversation-coach npm install @google/genai ``` Create .env.local: ```bash GEMINI_API_KEY=your_key GRADIUM_API_KEY=your_key ``` Suggested routes: - POST /api/transcribe — receive user audio; Gradium STT; return text - POST /api/converse — scenario + difficulty + conversation history + user message; Gemini; return reply - POST /api/speak — text; Gradium TTS; return playable WAV audio - POST /api/feedback — conversation transcript + scenario; Gemini; return structured feedback ## Gemini implementation example ```typescript import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai"; const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY, }); const response = await ai.models.generateContent({ model: "gemini-2.5-flash", contents: "I'd like to discuss a salary increase.", config: { systemInstruction: "You are a skeptical but fair manager. The user is practising asking for a raise. " + "Stay in character. Ask challenging but believable follow-up questions. " + "Respond in 1–3 natural spoken sentences. Do not coach until the session ends.", }, }); console.log(response.text); ``` For real conversations, send a chat session/history containing **all prior turns**, not only the latest utterance. Keep the role-play consistent with scenario, role and difficulty. Keep replies short to lower latency. ## Gradium voice integration API base: [https://api.gradium.ai](https://api.gradium.ai) - **Speech-to-text:** POST /api/post/speech/asr - **Text-to-speech:** POST /api/post/speech/tts - Follow current official REST request/response details; validate with one sample before building the whole UI. Example server-side TTS request: ```typescript const response = await fetch( "https://api.gradium.ai/api/post/speech/tts", { method: "POST", headers: { "x-api-key": process.env.GRADIUM_API_KEY!, "Content-Type": "application/json", }, body: JSON.stringify({ text: "Why do you believe you deserve a raise?", voice_id: "YTpq7expH9539ERJ", output_format: "wav", only_audio: true, }), } ); if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Gradium TTS failed"); const audio = await response.arrayBuffer(); ``` Return the WAV from the server to the browser with the correct audio content type. Choose an available voice ID from the Gradium docs/dashboard if the example changes. **Important STT gotcha:** MediaRecorder may output WebM/Opus in the browser. Do **not** label WebM as WAV. Either record/encode PCM WAV or convert correctly server-side. Parse the STT response according to the current Gradium docs (including NDJSON segments if returned), concatenating relevant recognised text. **Latency choice:** push-to-talk instead of continuous full-duplex streaming. Finish one turn, get text, generate response, synthesize and play audio, then resume listening. ## Cartoon avatar implementation **Fastest:** animated SVG / 2D character with subtle bobbing, periodic blink and a two-state mouth. Use CSS or Framer Motion if already installed. **If 3D is essential:** use one licensed premade GLB/VRM avatar + Three.js / React Three Fiber; a compatible VRM can use three-vrm for expressions. Frame the upper torso. Avoid the avatar editor entirely. Ready Player Me's former public offering should not be assumed available. A playful sunflower makes practice approachable; evidence-backed reports and repeat sessions make it useful. ### What we have now - **Rehearsal studio:** animated sunflower, scenario outfits in a wardrobe, Aura visualizer, focus/full-stage controls, and friendly, neutral or challenging counterparts. - **Eight scenarios:** job interview, asking for a raise, relationship breakup, difficult feedback, flatmate conversation, cold call, bazaar negotiation and a custom situation. - **Three ways to answer:** hands-free live voice with automatic turn taking and interruptions; manually recorded answers; typed messages. Both voice modes show an accumulating live transcript. - **Adaptive responses:** short in-character replies using conversation history. Wording-based tone detection changes expression and automatic voice choice; Marshall and Lainey are optional voice overrides. - **Detailed coaching:** strengths, improvements, suggested phrasing and scored dimensions with quoted evidence. Interview coaching adds target-role context, answer-by-answer reviews, a heatmap, one priority, a drill and the next session’s goal. “Practise this answer” starts a focused retry. - **Local profile and growth:** saved transcripts/reports, comparable-session trends, skill filters, recurring strengths and improvement themes linked to supporting reports, and a practice-completion tracker. Completing a drill records practice, not proof of improved performance. - **Recorded voice review:** microphone audio saved locally, separate verbatim transcription, hesitation counts, clickable timestamps, playback and frequency comparisons. Failed analysis can be retried while recordings remain playable. ### What changed from the original plan The push-to-talk prototype has grown into a **practise → review → retry → track progress** loop. We now have a distinctive sunflower/wardrobe experience, continuous voice, richer coaching and local history. Recorded audio is now retained for review; the original “no raw recordings” assumption is superseded. ### Current technical shape - Next.js, React and TypeScript; server routes keep provider keys out of browser code. - Gradium streaming STT → Gemini text reply → Gradium streamed TTS. Manual recording also has a final WAV transcription path. - Configured defaults in source: `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` for conversation, `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` for reports, and `gemini-3.5-transcribe` for recorded-audio review. Environment overrides can change these. - Reports live in the browser-local profile; WAV recordings live in IndexedDB. Latest 50 sessions retained, with linked audio removed on deletion/eviction. No accounts or cross-device sync. - Recording is capped at 10 minutes per session, split into clips of at most 60 seconds. Audio is sent to providers for processing; local storage does not mean offline processing. ### Verified now / still open **Fresh checks for this update:** 273 unit/API tests pass; TypeScript check passes. This supersedes the earlier 178-pass/17-fail audit. These tests use mocked providers. **Previously recorded evidence in README:** dedicated audio browser tests and synthetic live-provider checks passed. Those were not rerun for this documentation update; a full current browser suite and physical-microphone rehearsal are not newly verified. - [ ] Run one complete demo on the actual microphone/headset: start, interrupt, finish, review, replay and restart. Check echo and latency. - [ ] Run the full browser suite against the final integrated checkout; an earlier README run recorded a timing-sensitive live-transcript failure that passed in isolation. - [ ] Before a public live-voice demo, protect voice-token issuance. It currently accepts [localhost](http://localhost) only. **Interpretation limits:** tone comes from wording, not acoustic emotion detection. Scores, filler detection and timing are coaching estimates. Recurring themes need evidence from at least two comparable reports. Live feedback collection during conversation is not wired up; only its validated storage connector exists. ### Ideas / possible next steps These are proposals, not implemented features or agreed commitments. - **Immediate demo focus:** show one clear improvement loop, rather than touring every chart. Interview practice demonstrates the deepest coaching; bazaar negotiation is a quick playful opener. - **Live coaching cues:** connect the existing live-feedback connector to lightweight hints at appropriate moments, while keeping the counterpart in character. - **Personalised practice:** use recurring evidence to suggest the next scenario or drill and revisit the same question after practice. - **Recruitment direction from the original brainstorm:** voice-led profile discovery, identify what matters to the person, then filter and match jobs. This would be a separate expansion beyond conversation rehearsal. - **Broader personal dashboard from the original brainstorm:** voice-led goals, habits and plans. Keep this as a future direction until the core coaching loop is proven. **Demo outline:** Features For Demo --- ## Original brainstorm — retained Ideas; Recruitment agent, use voice chat to build profile, build something that actually matches you to jobs, filter out shit, personal recommendation about how you are feeling, what to do, plans, organise something voice chat, takes in info, asks lots of questions to get information on your profile, finds out what is important to you and builds on that, creates dashbaord for you track habits, plans, jobs, etc --- # Original four-hour build plan — historical reference The plan and checklists below preserve the initial approach and earlier audit context. ## Demo story
**“Practise the conversations that matter before having them for real.”**
Proposed walkthrough, based on the current local implementation. Updated <mention-date start="2026-10-10"/>.
### Main demo: practise → review → retry
1. **Choose the situation.** Open the sunflower wardrobe, select Job interview, set the difficulty and target role.
2. **Have a short conversation.** Start live voice and give two or three answers. Show the live transcript, spoken replies and sunflower states. Briefly demonstrate interruption if the microphone setup has been rehearsed.
3. **End and learn.** Open the coaching report. Expand one answer to show the original words, quoted evidence and one concrete improvement.
4. **Listen back.** Once audio analysis finishes, play the recording and click a detected hesitation timestamp, if present. Explain that these are estimates, not a perfect count of every filler.
5. **Try again.** Select “Practise this answer” and use the suggested improvement.
6. **Show progress.** Open My profile. With genuine comparable prior sessions, show trends and recurring themes. A first session will not have comparison evidence.
### Features worth highlighting
- A recognisable sunflower character with outfits tied to scenarios.
- Natural voice conversation using Gradium STT and streamed TTS.
- Separate fast conversation and richer coaching model paths.
- Feedback grounded in the user’s actual answers.
- Local saved reports, audio replay and targeted practice.
**Optional opener:** Bazaar negotiation for a short, playful exchange before showing the interview coaching depth.
### Before presenting
- [ ] Rehearse on the actual laptop and headset, including interruption, audio review and restart.
- [ ] Prepare genuine prior sessions at matching scenario/difficulty/role if showing progress.
- [ ] Check provider access and report/audio-analysis latency; analysis runs after coaching and may take longer.
- [ ] Use [localhost](http://localhost) for continuous voice unless protected public token issuance has been implemented.
- [ ] Keep typed input available if microphone capture fails; it demonstrates conversation and coaching but cannot demonstrate audio analysis.
### Claims to keep accurate
Fresh unit/API check: **273 tests pass**, and typecheck passes. This is not proof of a physical-microphone demo.
Profiles and recordings are local to this browser; processing still uses external providers. There are no accounts or cross-device sync. Tone adaptation is based on words; live in-conversation coaching cues remain a future idea.

## Demo story
**“Practise the conversations that matter before having them for real.”**
Proposed walkthrough, based on the current local implementation. Updated <mention-date start="2026-10-10"/>.
### Main demo: practise → review → retry
1. **Choose the situation.** Open the sunflower wardrobe, select Job interview, set the difficulty and target role.
2. **Have a short conversation.** Start live voice and give two or three answers. Show the live transcript, spoken replies and sunflower states. Briefly demonstrate interruption if the microphone setup has been rehearsed.
3. **End and learn.** Open the coaching report. Expand one answer to show the original words, quoted evidence and one concrete improvement.
4. **Listen back.** Once audio analysis finishes, play the recording and click a detected hesitation timestamp, if present. Explain that these are estimates, not a perfect count of every filler.
5. **Try again.** Select “Practise this answer” and use the suggested improvement.
6. **Show progress.** Open My profile. With genuine comparable prior sessions, show trends and recurring themes. A first session will not have comparison evidence.
### Features worth highlighting
- A recognisable sunflower character with outfits tied to scenarios.
- Natural voice conversation using Gradium STT and streamed TTS.
- Separate fast conversation and richer coaching model paths.
- Feedback grounded in the user’s actual answers.
- Local saved reports, audio replay and targeted practice.
**Optional opener:** Bazaar negotiation for a short, playful exchange before showing the interview coaching depth.
### Before presenting
- [ ] Rehearse on the actual laptop and headset, including interruption, audio review and restart.
- [ ] Prepare genuine prior sessions at matching scenario/difficulty/role if showing progress.
- [ ] Check provider access and report/audio-analysis latency; analysis runs after coaching and may take longer.
- [ ] Use [localhost](http://localhost) for continuous voice unless protected public token issuance has been implemented.
- [ ] Keep typed input available if microphone capture fails; it demonstrates conversation and coaching but cannot demonstrate audio analysis.
### Claims to keep accurate
Fresh unit/API check: **273 tests pass**, and typecheck passes. This is not proof of a physical-microphone demo.
Profiles and recordings are local to this browser; processing still uses external providers. There are no accounts or cross-device sync. Tone adaptation is based on words; live in-conversation coaching cues remain a future idea.

A playful sunflower makes practice approachable; evidence-backed reports and repeat sessions make it useful. ### What we have now - **Rehearsal studio:** animated sunflower, scenario outfits in a wardrobe, Aura visualizer, focus/full-stage controls, and friendly, neutral or challenging counterparts. - **Eight scenarios:** job interview, asking for a raise, relationship breakup, difficult feedback, flatmate conversation, cold call, bazaar negotiation and a custom situation. - **Three ways to answer:** hands-free live voice with automatic turn taking and interruptions; manually recorded answers; typed messages. Both voice modes show an accumulating live transcript. - **Adaptive responses:** short in-character replies using conversation history. Wording-based tone detection changes expression and automatic voice choice; Marshall and Lainey are optional voice overrides. - **Detailed coaching:** strengths, improvements, suggested phrasing and scored dimensions with quoted evidence. Interview coaching adds target-role context, answer-by-answer reviews, a heatmap, one priority, a drill and the next session’s goal. “Practise this answer” starts a focused retry. - **Local profile and growth:** saved transcripts/reports, comparable-session trends, skill filters, recurring strengths and improvement themes linked to supporting reports, and a practice-completion tracker. Completing a drill records practice, not proof of improved performance. - **Recorded voice review:** microphone audio saved locally, separate verbatim transcription, hesitation counts, clickable timestamps, playback and frequency comparisons. Failed analysis can be retried while recordings remain playable. ### What changed from the original plan The push-to-talk prototype has grown into a **practise → review → retry → track progress** loop. We now have a distinctive sunflower/wardrobe experience, continuous voice, richer coaching and local history. Recorded audio is now retained for review; the original “no raw recordings” assumption is superseded. ### Current technical shape - Next.js, React and TypeScript; server routes keep provider keys out of browser code. - Gradium streaming STT → Gemini text reply → Gradium streamed TTS. Manual recording also has a final WAV transcription path. - Configured defaults in source: `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` for conversation, `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` for reports, and `gemini-3.5-transcribe` for recorded-audio review. Environment overrides can change these. - Reports live in the browser-local profile; WAV recordings live in IndexedDB. Latest 50 sessions retained, with linked audio removed on deletion/eviction. No accounts or cross-device sync. - Recording is capped at 10 minutes per session, split into clips of at most 60 seconds. Audio is sent to providers for processing; local storage does not mean offline processing. ### Verified now / still open **Fresh checks for this update:** 273 unit/API tests pass; TypeScript check passes. This supersedes the earlier 178-pass/17-fail audit. These tests use mocked providers. **Previously recorded evidence in README:** dedicated audio browser tests and synthetic live-provider checks passed. Those were not rerun for this documentation update; a full current browser suite and physical-microphone rehearsal are not newly verified. - [ ] Run one complete demo on the actual microphone/headset: start, interrupt, finish, review, replay and restart. Check echo and latency. - [ ] Run the full browser suite against the final integrated checkout; an earlier README run recorded a timing-sensitive live-transcript failure that passed in isolation. - [ ] Before a public live-voice demo, protect voice-token issuance. It currently accepts [localhost](http://localhost) only. **Interpretation limits:** tone comes from wording, not acoustic emotion detection. Scores, filler detection and timing are coaching estimates. Recurring themes need evidence from at least two comparable reports. Live feedback collection during conversation is not wired up; only its validated storage connector exists. ### Ideas / possible next steps These are proposals, not implemented features or agreed commitments. - **Immediate demo focus:** show one clear improvement loop, rather than touring every chart. Interview practice demonstrates the deepest coaching; bazaar negotiation is a quick playful opener. - **Live coaching cues:** connect the existing live-feedback connector to lightweight hints at appropriate moments, while keeping the counterpart in character. - **Personalised practice:** use recurring evidence to suggest the next scenario or drill and revisit the same question after practice. - **Recruitment direction from the original brainstorm:** voice-led profile discovery, identify what matters to the person, then filter and match jobs. This would be a separate expansion beyond conversation rehearsal. - **Broader personal dashboard from the original brainstorm:** voice-led goals, habits and plans. Keep this as a future direction until the core coaching loop is proven. **Demo outline:** Features For Demo --- ## Original brainstorm — retained Ideas; Recruitment agent, use voice chat to build profile, build something that actually matches you to jobs, filter out shit, personal recommendation about how you are feeling, what to do, plans, organise something voice chat, takes in info, asks lots of questions to get information on your profile, finds out what is important to you and builds on that, creates dashbaord for you track habits, plans, jobs, etc --- # Original four-hour build plan — historical reference The plan and checklists below preserve the initial approach and earlier audit context. Use the current product summary above for present functionality, model choices, storage behaviour and verification. **Date:** 10 October 2026 **Concept:** An AI role-play simulator for conversations people find difficult. The user speaks out loud to a cartoon/metaverse-style character that answers naturally, challenges them, and gives specific feedback at the end. ## Product pitch **Practice the conversations that matter — before having them for real.** Examples: - Job interview with a realistic hiring manager - Asking a boss for a raise - Breaking up / navigating a difficult relationship conversation - Giving or receiving difficult workplace feedback - Negotiating, setting boundaries, apologising, or handling conflict - Custom user-provided scenario The differentiator is **interactive rehearsal and useful feedback**, not photorealistic avatar technology. ## Earlier implementation audit — superseded The earlier audit recorded 178 passing and 17 failing unit/API tests, browser regressions and typecheck errors while work was changing. The fresh unit/API and typecheck results above supersede those failures; final physical-microphone demo acceptance remains open. ## Scope: what we actually ship in four hours **Must have** - [x] Choose a scenario and difficulty (friendly / neutral / challenging) - [x] Display one premade cartoon avatar - [x] User speaks with live chat - [x] Gradium transcribes the user's speech - [x] Gemini generates a brief in-character response using conversation history - [x] Gradium turns the response into speech - [x] Avatar switches among idle, listening and speaking animations - [x] End Session generates a short feedback report **Originally cut / optional scope** Unchecked exclusions below are intentional scope cuts, not remaining MVP requirements. Continuous voice and reporting were subsequently added as noted. - [ ] Photorealistic lip-sync, body tracking or elaborate gestures - [ ] Authentication, payment, database or saved accounts - [x] Full-duplex voice interruptions and overlapping speech — subsequently implemented as local continuous voice with interruption handling; playback-interruption regression still needs verification. - [ ] Complex environments, multi-character scenes, multiplayer - [ ] Sophisticated analytics and long transcripts dashboard — partially exceeded: local profiles, saved transcripts, score trends, answer reviews and speech metrics exist; profile/report integration checks are still failing. Photo-to-avatar is not required for this MVP. A premade stylized character plus basic lip movement is sufficient for the demo. ## Proposed technology stack
Layer Technology Responsibility
UI Next.js + TypeScript + Tailwind Scenario picker, voice screen, results
Conversation brain Gemini Flash via @google/genai Role-play, follow-up questions, feedback
Voice recognition Gradium STT Convert user's mic audio to text
Voice generation Gradium TTS Read Gemini's answer in character
Avatar Animated 2D SVG **or** premade GLB/VRM Show idle/listening/speaking states
API orchestration Next.js route handlers Protect API keys; coordinate services
Media Browser microphone, HTMLAudioElement Capture/play voice audio
**Choice:** For a reliable four-hour build, prefer a polished animated 2D portrait. Use a premade 3D GLB/VRM only if it already loads and animates. Building an avatar engine is not the product. **Avoid Gemini Live for this particular prototype:** If Gradium must supply both STT and TTS, use Gemini for **text conversation**. Gemini Live's own native audio capabilities would duplicate part of the Gradium pipeline. ## End-to-end architecture 1. User selects scenario + difficulty. 2. Browser records one answer using push-to-talk. 3. POST recorded audio to server API route. 4. Backend sends supported audio to Gradium speech-to-text; obtains a transcript. 5. Backend sends transcript and previous conversation turns to Gemini. 6. Gemini replies as the chosen character, usually 1–3 spoken sentences; backend appends that turn to history. 7. Backend sends Gemini's reply to Gradium text-to-speech and receives audio. 8. Frontend plays the audio and switches avatar to **speaking**. 9. Playback ends; avatar returns to **idle/listening**. 10. User can repeat until they press **End Session**. 11. Gemini evaluates the transcript against a rubric and returns 2 strengths, 2 improvements and 1 suggested better response. **Conceptual flow:** User microphone → Gradium STT → Gemini Flash + history → Gradium TTS → spoken audio + animated avatar. ## Quick setup 1. Get a [Gemini API key](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey). 2. Get a [Gradium API key](https://studio.gradium.ai/). 3. Scaffold a Next.js project and install the Google GenAI SDK. 4. Keep keys on the backend. Never expose Gradium/Gemini keys through NEXT_PUBLIC environment variables. ```bash npx create-next-app@latest conversation-coach cd conversation-coach npm install @google/genai ``` Create .env.local: ```bash GEMINI_API_KEY=your_key GRADIUM_API_KEY=your_key ``` Suggested routes: - POST /api/transcribe — receive user audio; Gradium STT; return text - POST /api/converse — scenario + difficulty + conversation history + user message; Gemini; return reply - POST /api/speak — text; Gradium TTS; return playable WAV audio - POST /api/feedback — conversation transcript + scenario; Gemini; return structured feedback ## Gemini implementation example ```typescript import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai"; const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY, }); const response = await ai.models.generateContent({ model: "gemini-2.5-flash", contents: "I'd like to discuss a salary increase.", config: { systemInstruction: "You are a skeptical but fair manager. The user is practising asking for a raise. " + "Stay in character. Ask challenging but believable follow-up questions. " + "Respond in 1–3 natural spoken sentences. Do not coach until the session ends.", }, }); console.log(response.text); ``` For real conversations, send a chat session/history containing **all prior turns**, not only the latest utterance. Keep the role-play consistent with scenario, role and difficulty. Keep replies short to lower latency. ## Gradium voice integration API base: [https://api.gradium.ai](https://api.gradium.ai) - **Speech-to-text:** POST /api/post/speech/asr - **Text-to-speech:** POST /api/post/speech/tts - Follow current official REST request/response details; validate with one sample before building the whole UI. Example server-side TTS request: ```typescript const response = await fetch( "https://api.gradium.ai/api/post/speech/tts", { method: "POST", headers: { "x-api-key": process.env.GRADIUM_API_KEY!, "Content-Type": "application/json", }, body: JSON.stringify({ text: "Why do you believe you deserve a raise?", voice_id: "YTpq7expH9539ERJ", output_format: "wav", only_audio: true, }), } ); if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Gradium TTS failed"); const audio = await response.arrayBuffer(); ``` Return the WAV from the server to the browser with the correct audio content type. Choose an available voice ID from the Gradium docs/dashboard if the example changes. **Important STT gotcha:** MediaRecorder may output WebM/Opus in the browser. Do **not** label WebM as WAV. Either record/encode PCM WAV or convert correctly server-side. Parse the STT response according to the current Gradium docs (including NDJSON segments if returned), concatenating relevant recognised text. **Latency choice:** push-to-talk instead of continuous full-duplex streaming. Finish one turn, get text, generate response, synthesize and play audio, then resume listening. ## Cartoon avatar implementation **Fastest:** animated SVG / 2D character with subtle bobbing, periodic blink and a two-state mouth. Use CSS or Framer Motion if already installed. **If 3D is essential:** use one licensed premade GLB/VRM avatar + Three.js / React Three Fiber; a compatible VRM can use three-vrm for expressions. Frame the upper torso. Avoid the avatar editor entirely. Ready Player Me's former public offering should not be assumed available. Animation states: - **idle**: breathing/bobbing, occasional blink - **listening**: face forward, slight attentiveness - **speaking**: mouth toggles, small nod/head sway during TTS playback ```typescript audio.onplay = () => setIsSpeaking(true); audio.onended = () => setIsSpeaking(false); audio.onerror = () => setIsSpeaking(false); ``` This is an intentionally approximate speaking animation, not phoneme-accurate lip-sync. If there is no mouth blendshape, use an SVG mouth or simple mesh swap instead. ## Scenarios and persona instructions ### Job interview "You are an experienced interviewer assessing a candidate. Ask one question at a time. Demand specific examples and probe vague claims. Remain professional. Do not reveal a rubric or provide coaching until the session ends." ### Asking for a raise "You are the user's manager. You are skeptical but fair about salary increases. Ask for evidence of performance, impact and market value. Raise natural objections. Keep replies concise and conversational." ### Breakup or emotionally difficult conversation "You are the other party in a difficult but respectful relationship conversation. React in a believable, emotionally nuanced way while avoiding threats, manipulation or abuse. Let the user practise empathy and boundaries." ### Difficult feedback "You are a coworker receiving uncomfortable feedback. Start a little defensive, but become more receptive to clear, respectful and specific communication." ### Difficulty settings - **Friendly:** collaborative, gentle objections, lower pressure - **Neutral:** realistic responses and a few challenges - **Challenging:** probing objections, skepticism, follow-up questions without unnecessary hostility System instruction for every scenario: **Stay in character during practice; ask one question at a time; speak naturally in 1–3 sentences; do not prematurely deliver feedback.** A separate Gemini request should generate the final report. ## Interface / demo flow 1. **Landing:** "Practice difficult conversations with AI" 2. **Scenario cards:** Interview / Salary raise / Relationship / Difficult feedback / Custom 3. **Difficulty:** Friendly / Neutral / Challenging 4. **Conversation:** central cartoon avatar, animated state, push-to-talk mic button, small transcript, End Session 5. **Results:** two strengths, two improvements, recommended alternative phrasing; optionally restart at a harder difficulty Demo storyline: select **Ask for a Raise** → speak a salary request → manager challenges the justification by voice → respond once more → End Session → concise actionable report. ## Four-hour sprint checklist ### 00:00–00:45 — Gemini + skeleton UI - [x] Scaffold Next.js; create scenario picker - [x] Add /api/converse and persona prompts - [x] Verify a typed message gets an in-character Gemini response **Checkpoint:** text role-play works, even without voice. ### 00:45–01:40 — Gradium TTS - [x] Create /api/speak - [x] Turn a fixed sentence into playable speech - [x] Wire Gemini responses to automatic audio playback **Checkpoint:** click a button; character's response is heard. ### 01:40–02:35 — Microphone + STT - [x] Record short user turn - [x] Convert to compatible audio encoding - [x] Create /api/transcribe, parse recognized text - [x] Chain transcription → Gemini → TTS **Checkpoint:** complete two-way voice interaction works. ### 02:35–03:20 — Avatar animation - [x] Render one premade 2D or 3D avatar - [x] Implement idle/listening/speaking states - [x] Hook speaking state to TTS audio playback **Checkpoint:** avatar visibly responds when AI speaks. ### 03:20–04:00 — Feedback + reliability + demo - [x] Add the scenario/difficulty presets - [x] End Session report (2 strengths, 2 improvements, improved phrasing) - [x] Handle microphone denied, empty audio and failed API requests - [ ] Rehearse a complete 2-minute walkthrough **Checkpoint:** demo works from start to finish. ## What could go wrong / fallback plan - **STT audio incompatibility:** test encoding immediately; if blocked, temporarily allow typed input so the rest of the demo remains usable. - **3D avatar takes too long:** revert to a clean 2D SVG character. Animation quality is secondary. - **TTS latency:** keep Gemini replies short, use a loading/speaking state, and avoid huge transcripts per request. - **API quota or model problems:** test keys at the start, show recoverable errors, and have a prerecorded walkthrough/video only as backup for the presentation. - **Unsafe/awkward role-play:** give scenarios clear guardrails; keep relationship simulations respectful and clearly fictional. - **Privacy:** avoid storing raw recordings in MVP unless necessary; get consent if recording or keeping a transcript. ## Definition of done - [x] A user can select **Ask for a Raise** - [x] Their spoken words are recognized by Gradium - [x] Gemini responds in character based on conversation history - [x] Gradium delivers the response in a spoken voice - [x] A cartoon avatar animates when speaking - [x] User can complete at least three turns - [ ] End Session produces clear, useful feedback - [ ] One complete demo can run without editing source code or manually calling APIs ## Copy-paste prompt for Cursor / coding agent > Build a hackathon MVP called Conversation Coach using Next.js App Router, TypeScript and Tailwind. Users select an interview, salary negotiation, breakup conversation, or difficult feedback scenario. Gemini is the conversation AI, using @google/genai with gemini-2.5-flash and full multi-turn history. Gradium must handle both speech-to-text and text-to-speech using the documented REST endpoints. Implement server-side routes /api/transcribe, /api/converse, /api/speak, and /api/feedback; keep keys in GEMINI_API_KEY and GRADIUM_API_KEY server environment variables. Use browser push-to-talk recording, and ensure WAV compatibility for Gradium STT (do not send WebM marked as WAV). Parse Gradium STT responses correctly. Use Gradium TTS with WAV audio output and play it with an HTMLAudioElement. Build a playful, clean cartoon avatar UI with idle/listening/speaking states and simple mouth motion during playback. Prioritize a functional voice loop over complex 3D. Include friendly, neutral and challenging difficulty settings; keep Gemini in character with short spoken replies. Maintain conversation history. Add End Session feedback with 2 strengths, 2 improvements and a suggested better response from Gemini. Add loading, microphone and API error states. No database, authentication, payments, photo-to-avatar generation or unnecessary dependencies. Implement incrementally: text conversation first, then TTS, then STT, then avatar, then feedback. ## Documentation / links - [Gemini API keys](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey) - [Google GenAI / Gemini API](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content) - [Gradium Studio](https://studio.gradium.ai/) - [Gradium speech-to-text REST guide](https://docs.gradium.ai/guides/speech-to-text-rest) - [Gradium text-to-speech REST guide](https://docs.gradium.ai/guides/text-to-speech-rest) - [three-vrm for optional 3D avatar](https://github.com/pixiv/three-vrm) **Execution rule:** Do not spend the first two hours making the avatar pretty.
